items.title: EasyBI
items.text:
Self-service BI for WPF. You declare what can be analyzed; your users build their charts, tables and dashboards by drag and drop, inside your application.

Get started See the sample

items.title: In three steps
What your users get
items.text:
• A designer

    Fields dragged onto wells, a dozen types of visuals, a properties panel, undo and redo.

    The designer

  • Dashboards

    Visuals arranged and resized by drag and drop, filled by dragging fields, with global filters and cross-filtering.

    Dashboard

  • Their own measures

    Formulas such as SUM([Revenue]; [Region] = "North") / [Revenue], with an editor that suggests what can be written.

    Calculated measures

  • Your look

    Light and dark, following WPF UI or Material Design. English and French, switched at runtime.

    Theming

items.title: Built for developers
items.text:
• One query per visual, in your database. Filters, grouping, aggregates, sort and Top N stay in the IQueryable: with EF Core, one SQL statement per visual, whatever the size of the table.
  • Plain records and JSON. Visuals and reports are immutable records, saved in a documented, versioned format (easybi/v1).
  • Open everywhere. Lookless controls made of slots, rules on what users may change, your own chart connector and visual types.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
flowchart LR
  source["Your data<br/>IQueryable"] --> model["Semantic model<br/><i>you declare it</i>"]
  model --> visual["Visual<br/><i>users build it</i>"]
  visual --> query["Query<br/><i>in your database</i>"]
  query --> chart["Chart<br/><i>LiveCharts2, OxyPlot...</i>"]
Package Role EasyBI.Wpf The controls: designer, visual, dashboard, filter bar, field list. Brings EasyBI.Core (query engine, JSON) and EasyBI.Abstractions (the records). EasyBI.Renderers.LiveCharts2 Draws the charts with LiveCharts2. EasyBI.Renderers.OxyPlot Draws the same charts with OxyPlot. EasyBI.Themes.WpfUi Follows a WPF UI theme. EasyBI.Themes.MaterialDesign Follows a Material Design in XAML theme.

Versions

This site documents every published version: pick one in the selector at the top of the page. dev is the development branch, not yet released.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: Every version, with its breaking changes. EasyBI follows Semantic Versioning: while in 0.x, breaking changes bump the minor version. The report format (easybi/v1) stays backward compatible: a newer version opens older reports, and a report using a newer feature cannot be opened by an older version.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Cross-filtering: several selections with Ctrl+click, highlighted in their visual (#41).
  • Numeric filters: number dimensions and the measures of a visual compared with numbers (≥, <, between...) (#42).
  • Matrix crossing rows with columns, with totals at every level (#43).
  • Conditional formatting: rules, color scales, data bars and icons on the values of a measure (#44); chart points colored by them, and the zones of rules shaded (#45).
  • Donut, gauge and waterfall visual types (#46).
  • Tooltips customized by the end user (extra measures, template) and the developer (EasyBIContext.TooltipOpening) (#47).
  • Legends: position chosen per visual, long legends paged (#48).
  • Several axis fields shown as groups, and dimension values relabeled per visual (#50).
  • Formulas with dimensions: SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, DISTINCTCOUNT and IF, with conditions (SUM([Revenue]; [Region] = "North")) (#53).
  • Measures declared in code editable in the application: QueryableSemanticModel.Formula(...), and any model measure redefined in a report, with Restore (#54).
  • Redesigned calculated measure editor: colored formula, located problems, smart suggestions, catalog in tabs, operator keypad (#55).
  • Measures used in other formulas: a calculated measure can use the report's other measures; loops are refused (#56).
  • This documentation site, with a version per release.
  • Designer rules: every change of the visual being designed passes the designer's Rules, which look at the change (VisualChange: Changes(v => ...), FieldsChanged) and refuse it with a message; what they would refuse is shown unavailable beforehand. Also declared as behaviors: LockVisualTypeBehavior, LockFieldsBehavior, ReadOnlyDesignerBehavior, or one of the application's derived from DesignerRuleBehavior (#65).
  • Visual types described by their definition: VisualTypeDefinition gives a type's name, gallery section, wells (used, number of fields, name), tooltips, format and rules, and VisualTypeCatalog holds EasyBI's; the designer, the validation and the fields added to a visual follow it. The designer refuses a second category on a pie or a donut (#59).
  • Custom visual types: an application declares its own types (EasyBIContext.AddVisualType, or a renderer's RendererCapabilities.VisualTypes), with their wells, settings (VisualTypeDefinition.Options, read with GetTypeOption) and rules, and an icon by key ({bi:VisualTypeIconKey company.type}, a default one otherwise); it hides or changes EasyBI's types in EasyBIContext.VisualTypes. The designer refuses a measure beyond what a type takes (a second value on a pie), a visual tells which well misses or has too many fields, and a matrix takes four row fields as documented (#60).
  • Failed visuals explained: a visual whose query or renderer throws says it could not be displayed, with Retry and the details of what happened (to copy into a bug report) instead of the exception's message; EasyBIContext.VisualFailed lets the application log the failure, change the message or hide the details (#73).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• LiveCharts2: the labels under groups turn like other category labels instead of being skipped (#51).
  • Designer: the measure preview no longer cancels a query on every keystroke (#52).
  • Comparisons with the previous year: a period under way (this year, the last months, a range ending later, the current year or month clicked) is compared with the same days a year earlier, not with the whole period; a range without an end no longer takes in this year's data (#62).
  • Charts: an axis drawing bars starts at zero also when a line shares it (a year in bars and the year before as a line), and ends at zero for negative bars; OxyPlot no longer cuts negative bars (#63).
  • Theming: an EasyBIThemeMapping that maps ChartPaletteKey gives charts the design system's palette instead of EasyBI's (#64).
  • Nullable dates (DateTime?, DateOnly?, DateTimeOffset?) by year, quarter, month or day: EF Core can translate the query again (it failed with SQL Server, SQLite...), and missing dates form an empty period instead of the year 1; a missing date has no previous year.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text:
• ReportDesigner.Visual is two-way, like DashboardView.Document: setting it loads a visual (null starts a new one) and it receives every change of the end user; Edit and Clear are gone (#65).
  • FilterContext.Selection became Selections (one per visual), with SelectionOf, ClearSelection(visualId) and DescribeSelections; CrossFilter holds Elements (SelectedElement), its Values and filter-based constructor are gone and Filters is computed (#41).
  • The MarkType enum became VisualType, a type identified by its Id, so that applications can add their own; EasyBI's are static properties (VisualType.Bar...) listed in VisualType.BuiltIn, and code that switched on them compares them instead (type == VisualType.Bar). Renamed with it: VisualDefinition.Mark → Type, MeasureRef.Mark and ChartSeries.Mark → SeriesType, RendererCapabilities.Marks → Types, VisualPipeline.SeriesMark and MarksOf → SeriesType and TypesOf, and in the designer SelectedMark, MarkOptions, MarkGroups, SelectedMarkOption → SelectedType, TypeOptions, TypeGroups, SelectedTypeOption, MarkOptionViewModel → VisualTypeOptionViewModel, VisualTypeIcon.Mark → Type, the SeriesMark chip property → SeriesType. MarkGroup became VisualTypeGroup and moved with FormatTarget to EasyBI.Abstractions (#59).
  • Report JSON: a visual's mark became type and a measure's mark became seriesType. The schema stays easybi/v1 while EasyBI is in beta: in a report saved by an earlier version, rename these properties, otherwise its visuals open as bars (#59).
  • ChartLegend moved from EasyBI.Core to EasyBI.Abstractions and gained Auto, Top and Left; ChartFitting.BottomLegendHeight was removed (#48).
  • ModelField.IsEditable is true for every measure (the model's ones can be redefined); use IsReportMeasure for the report's own measures. MeasureContext.Set matches a measure by model and name (#54).
  • A formula using a measure that the report redefines now reads the report's version, the model's Formula measures included (#56).
  • FieldDescriptor gained an optional Formula positional parameter: source compatible, recompile (#54).

items.title: Report format
items.text: easybi/v1, backward compatible: AnyOf filters with alternatives; comparison operators (GreaterThan, Range...); the Matrix, Donut, Gauge and Waterfall marks with an optional gauge; format on a measure; showOnChart on a rule; tooltip, legendPosition and labels on a visual. A redefinition is a measures entry named like the model's measure. Formulas may use functions and other measures.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Modernized designer: a properties panel on the right for the selected field, filter or visual (extensible through DesignerViewModel.PropertiesBuilding), chips summed up by badges, a visual type gallery, wells that follow the visual type, undo / redo and keyboard shortcuts for the chips.
  • Customizable components: slots to add, replace or hide parts of the designer, filter bar, field list, filter editor and dashboard; the five components are lookless controls with replaceable templates.
  • Renderer options: renderers declare their own options, edited in the designer and saved with the visual; LiveCharts2 charts can scroll.
  • Designer: sort and Top N, search in the field list and in a filter's values, a message explaining why a field is refused.
  • Dashboard: item selection with the mouse and the keyboard, copy and paste with the layout (also between dashboards), moving and extending items with the keyboard, fewer columns on a narrow dashboard, only the visuals in or near view are queried.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text:
• ReportDesigner, FieldList, FilterBar, FilterEditor and DashboardView derive from Control instead of UserControl: code relying on their former named elements uses the new properties (ReportDesigner.ViewModel, FieldList.Dimensions...) and routed commands (FilterBar.AddFilterCommand...).
  • ReportDesigner has a new default template: the ReportDesignerSlots.Sort and RendererOptions slots are replaced by Properties; chip settings moved to the properties panel.
  • DesignerViewModel.CanDrop refuses fields on a well the visual type does not use.

items.title: Report format
items.text: easybi/v1 is unchanged: renderer settings live in the existing extensions of a visual. v0.3 files load as they are.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Calculated measures: Ratio(...) / Calculated(g => ...) for developers, and formulas end users write from the field list ([Margin] / [Revenue]), saved with the report.
  • Period filters: between two dates, or relative to today (this month, last 12 months, last year), in the designer and the filter bar.
  • Comparisons over time: previous year, change, % change, year to date per measure; KPI trends (▲ / ▼).
  • Data refresh and performance: EasyBIContext.RefreshData(model); leaner SQL GROUP BY (1.3× to 1.7× faster on SQLite with 5 million rows).

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text:
• VisualPipeline.PrepareAsync has a new optional measures parameter before the cancellation token: pass the token by name (cancellationToken: token).
  • FieldDescriptor, AnalyticQuery and ModelField gained optional positional parameters: source compatible, recompile code built against v0.2.

items.title: Report format
items.text: easybi/v1 stays backward compatible: new optional measures (report) and time (measure) properties, new filter operators Between, Current, Last, Previous. Files using them cannot be opened by v0.2.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Dashboard built from a panel, a layout API and behaviors (#10), laid out with greedy items and no gaps (#14); visuals built by dragging fields onto it (#15).
  • Combined charts: a chart type per measure, with a secondary value axis (#11).
  • Drag and drop infrastructure, reusable by applications (#13).
  • Themes: EasyBI light and dark, following WPF UI and Material Design (#17).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Small LiveCharts2 and OxyPlot charts stay readable (#12).

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: • Dashboards are laid out with greedy items in rows and columns instead of a grid with gaps (#14).

items.title: 0.1.0-beta.1 — 2026-10-16
items.text:
First published version.

  • Semantic models over IQueryable, query engine pushing filters, grouping, aggregates, sort and top to the provider.
  • Designer, visuals, LiveCharts2 and OxyPlot connectors.
  • Global filters and cross-filtering (#2).
  • English and French, with runtime language switching (#4).
  • NuGet packages published with Trusted Publishing (#3, #5).

items.title: Writing this documentation
items.text:
This site is built from the Markdown files of the docs folder with Zensical, and published on GitHub Pages:

  • Every page has an edit button that opens its Markdown file on GitHub. A change merged into develop updates the dev version of the site within minutes; nothing has to be uploaded by hand.
  • Each release tag (vX.Y.Z) publishes its own version, which becomes latest; older versions stay available in the version selector.
  • A change to the public API or to the report format updates the page that documents it, and adds an entry to the changelog under Unreleased (with Breaking changes when there are).

To preview the site locally:

pip install zensical
zensical serve

items.title: Getting started
items.text: In ten minutes: a WPF window that shows a chart of your data, then a designer where your users build their own.

items.title: 1. Install
2. Describe your data
items.text:
A semantic model tells EasyBI what can be analyzed in a collection: its dimensions (what you group by: a region, a date...) and its measures (what you add up: a revenue, a quantity...).

public sealed record Sale(DateTime Date, string Region, string Channel,
                          decimal Amount, int Quantity);

var model = SemanticModel.For(sales, "sales", "Sales") // (1)!
    .Dimension(s => s.Date, "Date")
    .Dimension(s => s.Region, "Region")
    .Dimension(s => s.Channel, "Channel")
    .Measure(s => s.Amount, "Revenue", format: "#,##0 €") // (2)!
    .Measure(s => s.Quantity, "Quantity")
    .Count("Number of sales");
  1. sales is any IEnumerable<Sale> or IQueryable<Sale>: a list in memory, or a table of EF Core. "sales" is the name reports use, "Sales" the caption users see.
  2. A measure is summed by default; users can switch it to an average, a minimum...

The semantic model page covers everything a model can declare, and how to plug a database.

items.title: 3. Create the context
items.text:
The context gathers your models and the renderers that draw the charts. Create one for the application, and keep it: every EasyBI control of the application uses it.

public partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    public EasyBIContext Context { get; } = EasyBIContext.Create()
        .AddModel(model)
        .UseRenderer(new LiveCharts2Renderer());

    public MainWindow()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        DataContext = this;
    }
}

items.title: 4. Show a chart
items.text:
A visual says what to show: the model, the type of chart, the fields on each axis. A VisualView draws it.

XAMLC# 
<Window xmlns:bi="https://github.com/TheoCvg/EasyBI" ...>
    <bi:VisualView Context="{Binding Context}" Definition="{Binding RevenueByRegion}" />
</Window>

public VisualDefinition RevenueByRegion { get; } = new()
{
    Title = "Revenue by region",
    Model = "sales",
    Type = VisualType.Bar,
    Axis = [new("Region")],                     // (1)!
    Values = [new("Amount")],                   // (2)!
    Sort = new("Amount", Descending: true),
};
  1. Fields are referred to by name: the member name by default (Region, Product.Category).
  2. Amount is the measure captioned "Revenue".

Run the application: the chart of the top of this page shows. The query runs in the background, grouped and summed by the model (in SQL with EF Core), so only the five totals reach the chart.

items.title: 5. Let your users design
items.text:
Replace the hard-coded visual with a designer: users drag fields, pick a type, and the visual follows.

<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}" Visual="{Binding RevenueByRegion}" />

Visual is two-way: what users build comes back into your property. See The designer.

items.title: 6. Save and open reports
items.text:
Visuals and reports are plain records, saved as JSON (the easybi/v1 format):

var report = new ReportDefinition { Title = "Sales", Visuals = [RevenueByRegion] };
File.WriteAllText("sales.json", ReportSerializer.Serialize(report));

var opened = ReportSerializer.Deserialize(File.ReadAllText("sales.json"));

{
  "schema": "easybi/v1",
  "title": "Sales",
  "visuals": [
    { "title": "Revenue by region", "model": "sales", "type": "Bar", "axis": [ { "field": "Region" } ], ... }
  ]
}

See the report format.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• Dashboard

    Several visuals, arranged by your users, with cross-filtering.

  • Filtering

    A filter bar for the whole dashboard, and clicks on a chart that filter the others.

  • Calculated measures

    Ratios and formulas, written by you or by your users.

  • The sample

    Everything together: dotnet run --project samples/EasyBI.Sample.

About the sample

The sample starts in your system language (English or French) and has a language picker in its toolbar. Its data picker switches the same sales between memory (20,000 rows) and a SQLite database of 1 or 5 million rows, created once in %LOCALAPPDATA%\EasyBI.Sample; the toolbar shows how long the last refresh took.

items.title: Writing a connector
items.text:
A connector draws EasyBI's visuals with a charting library. EasyBI comes with two, which draw the same visual their own way:

EasyBI does The connector does Queries, pivots, sorts, applies filters and time calculations Draws request.Chart with its library Picks the renderer for each visual Declares the types it draws Builds tooltips, legends' pages, colors of conditional formats Shows them, from request Turns clicks into cross-filtering Reports clicks with request.Select

A connector implements a single interface. It receives already queried and pivoted data (request.Chart: categories + series) and the raw ResultSet if needed:

public sealed class MyRenderer : IVisualRenderer
{
    public string Name => "MyLib";
    public RendererCapabilities Capabilities { get; } = new(new HashSet<VisualType> { VisualType.Bar });
    public FrameworkElement Render(RenderRequest request) { /* request.Chart.Categories, request.Chart.Series */ }
}

A connector can also draw a type of its own, which it declares in Capabilities.VisualTypes: see Custom visual types.

Each ChartSeries comes with its resolved SeriesType and SecondaryAxis: a connector draws every series with its own type, so one chart can mix bars, lines, areas and points.

Colors come from request.Theme: series take ColorAt(index), text Foreground, axis labels MutedForeground, grid lines GridLine, tooltips Background (each one null when the theme does not set it: keep the library's default). Draw on a transparent background, so that the chart sits on the theme's surface.

Tooltips are EasyBI's: a connector replaces its library's tooltip (or tracker) with a ChartTooltipHost (EasyBI.Wpf), and shows in it, while the pointer moves over the chart, the content of the hovered category and series:

var tooltip = new ChartTooltipHost(view);
view.MouseMove += (_, e) => tooltip.Show(HitTest(e.GetPosition(view)) is { } hit
    ? request.TooltipFor(hit.Category, [hit.Series])   // EasyBI.Core: the visual's settings and the application's changes
    : null);                                           // null hides it

Legends follow ChartFitting (EasyBI.Core), which gives the place of the legend and its pages for the chart's size, the visual's choice (request.Visual.LegendPosition) and the size of the library's entries (LegendMetrics). The host turns the pages through request.LegendPager: a connector shows the entries of its page and fits again when it changes.

void Fit()
{
    var fit = ChartFitting.Cartesian(request.Chart, view.ActualWidth, view.ActualHeight, request.Visual.LegendPosition, MyMetrics);
    var shown = ChartFitting.LegendEntries(fit, request.LegendPager);   // also tells the pager where the legend is
    for (var i = 0; i < series.Count; i++) series[i].ShowInLegend = shown(i);
}
view.SizeChanged += (_, _) => Fit();
if (request.LegendPager is { } pager) pager.Changed += (_, _) => Fit();

EasyBIContext.ResolveRenderer negotiates capabilities: the active renderer if it supports every type the visual uses (the visual's and its measures'), otherwise another plugged-in renderer, otherwise a built-in one. The designer disables the types that no renderer can draw.

items.title: Renderer options
items.text:
A connector offers settings of its own to the end user by declaring them in its capabilities: the designer shows them in the "Options" section of its properties panel (DesignerPropertySections.Options) for the visuals they apply to, as a check box, a list or a number box, and saves their values with the visual.

public RendererCapabilities Capabilities { get; } = new(marks)
{
    Options =
    [
        RendererOption.Toggle("scrollable", () => Strings.Scrollable, appliesTo: v => v.Type.IsCartesian()),
        RendererOption.Choice("curve", () => Strings.Curve, [new("straight", () => Strings.Straight), new("smooth", () => Strings.Smooth)]),
        RendererOption.Number("barWidth", () => Strings.BarWidth, 48, minimum: 4, maximum: 120),
    ],
};

public FrameworkElement Render(RenderRequest request)
{
    var scrollable = request.Visual.GetRendererOption<bool>(Name, "scrollable");   // EasyBI.Core
    ...
}
  • Labels are functions, read when shown, so that they follow the EasyBI language (EasyBILocalization.UICulture).
  • Values are stored in VisualDefinition.Extensions, one JSON object per renderer under its name ("LiveCharts2": "{\"scrollable\":true}"); a value equal to the option's default is not stored. The settings of a renderer are kept while another one draws the visual. WithRendererOption sets one in code.
  • The LiveCharts2 connector offers Scroll bar (LiveCharts2Renderer.ScrollableOption) on cartesian charts: the chart shows the first 20 categories (ScrollWindow) above a small chart of all of them, where a band marks the visible ones; dragging on it scrolls, the mouse wheel on the chart zooms.

items.title: Localization
items.text:
EasyBI's own texts (designer, filter bar, messages, granularity and aggregation names, blank and boolean values) ship in English and French. The language can change at runtime: designer, filter bar and visuals update immediately.

EasyBILocalization.Culture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("fr-FR"); // null = follow CurrentUICulture

The same culture formats numbers and dates. Your semantic model captions can follow the language too: call Localize with your own resources, and every caption becomes a resource key (a missing key falls back to the caption itself).

var model = SemanticModel.For(db.Sales, "sales", "Sales")
    .Dimension(s => s.Region, "Region")
    .Measure(s => s.Amount, "Revenue")
    .Localize(MyStrings.ResourceManager);

Your own XAML texts can follow it as well with LocalizedStrings and the Localize markup extension:

public static LocalizedStrings Texts { get; } = new(MyStrings.ResourceManager);

<Button Content="{bi:Localize Save, Source={x:Static local:App.Texts}}" />

Visual and report titles are user content: they are stored as typed and not translated.

items.title: Customizing the components: slots
items.text:
The parts of the ReportDesigner, FieldList, FilterBar, FilterEditor and DashboardView are slots: named places where an application adds its own content (before or after the default content), replaces it, or hides it.

<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}">
    <bi:Slots.Items>
        <!-- Under the preview -->
        <bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.Preview}">
            <Button Content="Publish" Command="{Binding DataContext.PublishCommand, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=Window}}" />
        </bi:Slot>
        <bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.Title}" Mode="Before"><TextBlock Text="Title:" /></bi:Slot>
        <bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.FiltersShelf}" Mode="Hide" />
    </bi:Slots.Items>
</bi:ReportDesigner>

Slots.Add(designer, ReportDesignerSlots.Header, exportButton);              // after the default content
Slots.Add(designer, ReportDesignerSlots.Fields, help, SlotMode.Before);      // above the field list
Slots.Add(filterBar, FilterBarSlots.AddButton, myAddButton, SlotMode.Replace);
Slots.Hide(designer, ReportDesignerSlots.FieldPanel);

items.title: Modes
items.text:
SlotMode Your content goes After (default) After the default content: on its right, or below it in a vertical slot (Fields, Shelves, Preview) Before Before it: on its left, or above it Replace Instead of it Hide Nowhere: the part disappears

Several slots with the same name show in declaration order; the last Replace or Hide wins.

items.title: Names
items.text:
Component ...Slots ReportDesigner FieldPanel, Fields, Header (with Title, VisualTypes), Shelves (with AxisShelf, LegendShelf, ValuesShelf, TooltipShelf, FiltersShelf), Preview, Properties FieldList Model, Search, Dimensions, Measures, AddMeasureButton FilterBar Filters, Label, Slicer, AddButton, Selection FilterEditor Values, Period DashboardView Body, ItemContent, EmptyItemChoices, ItemToolbar

The band menu of a dashboard is a menu, not a slot: change it in BandMenuBehavior.MenuOpening.

items.title: Data context
items.text:
Your content takes the data context of the place it shows in:

Where Data context The designer Its DesignerViewModel ({Binding Visual.Title}...) The filter bar, the field list The application's FilterBarSlots.Slicer The SlicerViewModel of a global filter The filter editor The FilterItemViewModel The dashboard item slots The DashboardItem (DashboardCommands act on it)

To reach your window's view-model from the designer: {Binding DataContext.MyCommand, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=Window}}.

items.title: Repeated slots take a template
items.text:
An element can only be shown once. A slot shown several times (FilterBarSlots.Slicer once per global filter, the dashboard item slots once per item, slots declared for several components) takes a ContentTemplate, applied to the data context of each place:

Slots.AddTemplate(dashboard, DashboardSlots.ItemToolbar, (DataTemplate)FindResource("ExportButton"));

items.title: Inheritance
items.text: Slots.Items is inherited: slots declared on a window or a panel apply to every component in it, and the nearest declaration replaces the others. The designer opened to edit a dashboard visual takes the slots of the dashboard.

items.title: Your own templates
items.text:
The components are lookless controls. Their default templates (Themes/*.xaml of EasyBI.Wpf) are built from SlotHosts (<bi:SlotHost Slot="..." Orientation="Vertical"> with the default content inside), so a template of yours keeps the slots it hosts. A template works with the components' read-only properties and commands:

Component For templates ReportDesigner Its ViewModel (DesignerViewModel), the template's data context FieldList ModelOptions, Dimensions, Measures, CanAddMeasure, AddMeasureCommand, EditMeasureCommand, DeleteMeasureCommand, ResetMeasureCommand (with ModelField.IsEditable, IsReportMeasure, IsRedefined) FilterBar Slicers, SelectionDescription, AddFilterCommand, RemoveFilterCommand (on the slicer of its data context), ClearSelectionCommand DashboardView Panel, DashboardCommands

items.title: Theming
items.text:
Every EasyBI control (designer, dashboard, filter bar, field list, KPI and table renderers, chart connectors) draws with resources looked up dynamically: an application restyles EasyBI by defining them, and switches theme at runtime by replacing the dictionary that defines them. Charts follow too, without querying their data again.

EasyBI, lightEasyBI, darkWPF UIMaterial DesignYour colors

The accent, the chart palette and the corner radius overridden: see below.

items.title: Light and dark
items.text:
<Application.Resources>
    <ResourceDictionary>
        <ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>
            <bi:EasyBIThemeDictionary Mode="Dark" />
        </ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>
    </ResourceDictionary>
</Application.Resources>

Without it, the light theme applies. To switch at runtime, change Mode (or swap the dictionary):

foreach (var theme in Application.Current.Resources.MergedDictionaries.OfType<EasyBIThemeDictionary>())
    theme.Mode = EasyBIThemeMode.Light;

items.title: Overriding a few colors
items.text:
Define the keys you want in your resources, after the theme dictionary; the others keep the theme's values:

<SolidColorBrush x:Key="{x:Static bi:EasyBITheme.AccentBrushKey}" Color="#7C3AED" />
<bi:ChartPalette x:Key="{x:Static bi:EasyBITheme.ChartPaletteKey}">
    <Color>#7C3AED</Color>
    <Color>#F59E0B</Color>
    <Color>#10B981</Color>
</bi:ChartPalette>
<CornerRadius x:Key="{x:Static bi:EasyBITheme.CornerRadiusKey}">4</CornerRadius>

The complete list, with their light and dark values, is in Themes/Light.xaml and Themes/Dark.xaml:

Key (EasyBITheme.…) Used for BackgroundBrushKey behind the dashboard, the designer and the visual editor SurfaceBrushKey cards (dashboard items, designer preview), popups, toolbars, chart tooltips SurfaceAltBrushKey field lists, designer shelves, empty items, alternate table rows BorderBrushKey, BorderStrongBrushKey borders and separators; empty items and free spaces ForegroundBrushKey, MutedForegroundBrushKey, DisabledForegroundBrushKey text, secondary text (headers, hints, icons, axis labels), unavailable options AccentBrushKey, AccentHoverBrushKey, AccentForegroundBrushKey selection, "+" buttons, drop indicators, and the text on them AccentSoftBrushKey, AccentSoftBorderBrushKey field chips, selection chip, drop placeholders SecondarySoftBrushKey, SecondarySoftBorderBrushKey filter chips HoverBrushKey small buttons under the pointer ErrorBrushKey error messages, bad values of conditional formats SuccessBrushKey, WarningBrushKey good and middle values of conditional formats MeasureBrushKey the Σ of measures in field lists, measures in formulas FormulaFunctionBrushKey, FormulaDimensionBrushKey, FormulaTextBrushKey, FormulaNumberBrushKey the parts of a formula in the calculated measure editor (EasyBI's values in the Material Design and WPF UI mappings) GridLineBrushKey grid lines of charts and tables ChartPaletteKey (ChartPalette) colors of chart series, in order CornerRadiusKey (CornerRadius) rounding of cards

Control-specific parts have their own style keys (DashboardOverlay.PlusButtonStyleKey, FreeSpaceStyleKey, DropPlaceholderStyleKey, DragSource.PreviewStyleKey... see Dashboard and Drag and drop), and DashboardItem has an implicit style.

items.title: Standard controls
items.text: Buttons, combo boxes, text boxes and check boxes inside EasyBI have no explicit style: they take your application's implicit styles, so a control library (WPF UI, Material Design...) styles them too. EasyBI's own light and dark themes color EasyBI's surfaces, text and charts, not the standard controls: with the dark theme and no control library, they keep the system's light look.

items.title: Following a control library
items.text:
With WPF UI or Material Design in XAML, install the matching package and merge its dictionary after the library's: EasyBI's surfaces, text, accent and charts then take the library's colors, light or dark, and follow its theme switches (ApplicationThemeManager.Apply, PaletteHelper.SetTheme). Its classes are in the bi: XAML namespace.

<!-- dotnet add package EasyBI.Themes.WpfUi -->
<ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>
    <ui:ThemesDictionary Theme="Dark" />
    <ui:ControlsDictionary />
    <bi:WpfUiTheme />
</ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>

<!-- dotnet add package EasyBI.Themes.MaterialDesign -->
<ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>
    <md:BundledTheme BaseTheme="Dark" PrimaryColor="DeepPurple" SecondaryColor="Lime" />
    <ResourceDictionary Source="pack://application:,,,/MaterialDesignThemes.Wpf;component/Themes/MaterialDesign3.Defaults.xaml" />
    <bi:MaterialDesignTheme />
</ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>

WpfUiTheme.Map and MaterialDesignTheme.Map list which library resource each EasyBI key takes. For another library or an application's own design system, derive from EasyBIThemeMapping and map the keys you need; unmapped keys keep EasyBI's light values, while the keys listed in Kept (colors the system has no equivalent for, such as Material Design's success and warning) and the chart palette follow the mapped background (EasyBI's light or dark values). A design system with its own chart colors maps ChartPaletteKey to its ChartPalette. If the library switches theme by swapping dictionaries without notifying, call Refresh() on the mapping afterwards.

ApplicationThemeManager.Apply sets the main window's Background itself: put an EasyBI background on the window's root panel rather than on the window (as the sample does).

public sealed class MyTheme() : EasyBIThemeMapping(new Dictionary<ComponentResourceKey, object>
{
    [EasyBITheme.BackgroundBrushKey] = "MyWindowBrush",
    [EasyBITheme.AccentBrushKey] = "MyPrimaryBrush",
});

items.title: Charts
items.text: VisualView passes the theme to renderers in RenderRequest.Theme (BiTheme): the palette, and the Foreground, MutedForeground, GridLine and Background colors (hexadecimal, null when unknown). It is built by EasyBITheme.ChartTheme(element) from the resources above. A palette or colors set on EasyBIContext.Theme take precedence over the resources.

items.title: Custom visual types
items.text: A visual type is a VisualType (an id) and its VisualTypeDefinition: its name, its section of the designer's gallery, the fields each well takes, its tooltips, its settings and its rules. EasyBI's own types (VisualType.Bar, VisualType.Pie...) are defined the same way, in the context's catalog (EasyBIContext.VisualTypes), so a type of the application goes through the same paths: the gallery, the wells, the properties panel, the validation, the fields dropped on a dashboard, cross-filtering and tooltips.

items.title: Declaring a type
items.text:
public static class BusinessTypes
{
    public static readonly VisualType Treemap = new("barista.treemap");

    public static VisualTypeDefinition TreemapDefinition { get; } = new(Treemap, () => Texts.Treemap)
    {
        Group = VisualTypeGroup.Composition,                          // section of the gallery; null: not offered
        Axis = new() { MinFields = 1, MaxFields = 2, Caption = () => Texts.Groups },
        Legend = VisualWell.Unused,
        Values = new() { MinFields = 1, MaxFields = 1, Caption = () => Texts.Size },
        HasTooltips = true,                                           // the tooltip well, and its measures queried
        Format = FormatTarget.Chart,                                  // the format settings of its values
        Options = [RendererOption.Toggle("labels", () => Texts.ShowLabels, @default: true)],
        Validate = v => v.Top is > 50 ? Texts.TooManyRectangles : null,
    };
}

var context = EasyBIContext.Create()
    .AddModel(sales)
    .AddVisualType(BusinessTypes.TreemapDefinition)
    .UseRenderer(new LiveCharts2Renderer())
    .UseRenderer(new TreemapRenderer());
  • The id has a prefix (barista.treemap), so that it never takes the name of a type EasyBI adds later: AddVisualType refuses an id without one. The id is what the report saves ("type": "barista.treemap"): keep it stable.
  • Captions are functions, read each time, so that they follow the language of EasyBI (see Localization).
  • Wells: IsUsed (a well the type does not use refuses fields), MinFields, MaxFields (null: no limit) and the name the designer gives the well (null: Axis, Legend or Values). The designer refuses a field beyond MaxFields, and the visual tells what is missing or too much. By default a type takes up to three axis fields, one legend and at least one measure.
  • Validate is a rule of the type, checked before the wells, so that its message, more precise, comes first.
  • Options are settings of the type, shown in the Options section of the properties panel whatever the renderer drawing it, and saved in the visual's Extensions under the type's id. The renderer reads them with visual.GetTypeOption<bool>("labels", true).

items.title: Drawing it
items.text:
A renderer draws the type when its capabilities list it, like any type (see Writing a connector). It receives the usual RenderRequest: the query result (Result) and the pivoted data (Chart: one category per axis value, one series per measure and legend value). It reports clicks with request.Select(new CategorySelection(...)), which cross-filters the other visuals, and shows tooltips with request.TooltipFor(category, series).

public sealed class TreemapRenderer : IVisualRenderer
{
    public string Name => "Treemap";

    public RendererCapabilities Capabilities { get; } = new(new HashSet<VisualType> { BusinessTypes.Treemap })
    {
        // Optional: declared with the renderer, so that plugging it in is enough
        VisualTypes = [BusinessTypes.TreemapDefinition],
    };

    public FrameworkElement Render(RenderRequest request) => new TreemapView(request);
}

When the renderer lists the definition in VisualTypes, UseRenderer declares the type, unless the catalog already has it: a library of visuals is plugged in with one call. The sample application's RankingRenderer is a complete example: a ranking of a dimension's items by a measure, with a setting, its icon, cross-filtering and tooltips. Without a renderer for it, the type is greyed in the gallery, and its visuals say that no renderer draws them.

items.title: Its icon
items.text:
The gallery shows the icon of a type from the resources: a Geometry drawn with the foreground in a 16×16 box, under the key of the type. Without one, the type shows a default icon. The same key replaces the icon of one of EasyBI's types.

<Application.Resources>
    <Geometry x:Key="{bi:VisualTypeIconKey barista.treemap}">M1.5,1.5 H9 V14.5 H1.5 Z M10,1.5 H14.5 V8 H10 Z M10,9 H14.5 V14.5 H10 Z</Geometry>
    <Geometry x:Key="{bi:VisualTypeIconKey Bar}">M2,14 V6 M6,14 V2 M10,14 V8 M14,14 V4</Geometry>
</Application.Resources>

In code, the key is VisualTypeIcons.KeyOf(type).

items.title: Changing EasyBI's types
items.text:
The catalog of the context changes EasyBI's types too, before the designer shows:

var types = context.VisualTypes;
types.Hide(VisualType.Waterfall);                                     // out of the gallery; its visuals still show
types.Replace(types.Get(VisualType.Bar) with { Caption = () => Texts.Columns });
Keep only a few types

Hide every other type of the gallery, after the renderers are plugged in (a renderer may bring types of its own):

VisualType[] kept = [VisualType.Bar, VisualType.Line, VisualType.Pie];
foreach (var type in context.VisualTypes.Definitions
             .Where(d => d.Group is not null && !kept.Contains(d.Type))
             .Select(d => d.Type).ToList())   // Hide changes the catalog being read
    context.VisualTypes.Hide(type);

For a single designer, a rule greys the other types instead.

A report written by another application can hold a type this one does not declare: it opens, and the visual says that no renderer draws it.

items.title: What a type cannot do yet
items.text:
• Have other wells than Axis, Legend and Values (a size and a color, for instance).
  • Show its own content without querying a model, like the text and image visuals.
  • Get its data in another shape than the result and the pivoted chart data: a renderer needing another shape builds it from request.Result.

items.title: Dashboard
items.text:
A dashboard shows several visuals that users arrange themselves: they drag fields onto it to make visuals, move and resize them, filter them all at once, and click a chart to filter the others.

Control Role 1 FilterBar Global filters and the summary of the selections: see Filters. 2 FieldList The fields to drag onto the dashboard to make visuals. 3 DashboardView The visuals, texts and images, arranged in bands.

items.title: Show it
items.text:
<DockPanel bi:VisualView.FilterContext="{Binding Filters}"> <!-- (1)! -->
    <bi:FilterBar DockPanel.Dock="Top" Context="{Binding Context}" />
    <bi:FieldList DockPanel.Dock="Left" Width="210" Context="{Binding Context}" />
    <bi:DashboardView Context="{Binding Context}" Document="{Binding Dashboard}" /> <!-- (2)! -->
</DockPanel>
  1. Shared by the filter bar and every visual: global filters and cross-filtering.
  2. Two-way: every change users make comes back into Dashboard, a DashboardDocument.

Each part is optional: a dashboard without a field list is arranged with its "+" buttons, one without a filter context does not cross-filter.

items.title: Save and open
items.text:
A DashboardDocument is the report (easybi/v1: visuals, filters, calculated measures) and its layout. It is saved as JSON, with the schema easybi-dashboard/v1:

BoundCode-behind 
public DashboardDocument Dashboard { get; set; } = new();   // bound to Document

File.WriteAllText(path, DashboardSerializer.Serialize(Dashboard));
Dashboard = DashboardSerializer.Deserialize(File.ReadAllText(path));

File.WriteAllText(path, DashboardSerializer.Serialize(dashboard.Capture()));
dashboard.Load(DashboardSerializer.Deserialize(File.ReadAllText(path)));   // (1)!
  1. A new undo history starts. DocumentLoaded is raised.

Plain reports open too

DashboardSerializer.Deserialize also reads an easybi/v1 report without a layout: its visuals get a default one. The layout is a WPF matter and never goes into the report itself.

items.title: Read-only
items.text:
<bi:DashboardView Context="{Binding Context}" Document="{Binding Dashboard}" IsReadOnly="True" />

No editing chrome, no editing command, no selection. Clicks keep cross-filtering. IsReadOnly is inherited, so item templates can use it.

items.title: Performance
items.text:
Only the visuals in or near the visible part of the dashboard query their data; the others query when they scroll into view. A change of filters or data costs them one query then.

Property ViewportMargin How far ahead items load, in viewport sizes (1 by default: a screen above and below). LoadsVisibleItemsOnly false loads every visual, to print or export the whole dashboard.
