items.title: Customizing the dashboard
items.text: The DashboardView owns the content and the layout; every interaction is a behavior you can configure, replace or remove. Events let your application take over dialogs or veto changes; commands and styles let you rebuild its look.

items.title: Behaviors
Events
Commands
items.text:
DashboardCommands trigger every action from your own buttons and templates (commands acting on an item take the item containing them):

AddVisual, AddText, AddImage, EditItem, RemoveItem, ResetSize, AddRight, AddBelow, InsertBand, RemoveBand, Duplicate, MoveItem, MoveItemToNewBand, ExtendItem.

<Button Content="Move down" Command="{x:Static bi:DashboardCommands.MoveItem}" CommandParameter="Below" />

The standard ApplicationCommands work too: Delete, SelectAll, Copy, Cut, Paste, Undo, Redo.

items.title: Slots
Styles and templates
items.text:
• DashboardView is lookless: its default template shows its Panel in a scroll viewer, under an AdornerDecorator where behaviors draw. A template of yours shows the panel with <ContentPresenter Content="{Binding Panel, RelativeSource={RelativeSource TemplatedParent}}" />.
  • DashboardItem is lookless too, with an implicit style; IsSelected (the default template draws a ring) and IsInViewport are there for templates.
  • The controls behaviors draw take styles under DashboardOverlay keys: PlusButtonStyleKey, IconButtonStyleKey, GripStyleKey, ResizeGripStyleKey, FreeSpaceStyleKey, DropPlaceholderStyleKey, DragGhostStyleKey, SelectionBoxStyleKey.

items.title: Drag and drop in your controls
items.text:
The drag and drop of the designer and the field list is built on reusable attached properties (namespace EasyBI.Wpf.DragAndDrop, XAML prefix bi:), usable on any ItemsControl of an application. Being attached properties, they can be set from a style:

<!-- Items can be dragged: a preview follows the pointer, a moved item is dimmed -->
<ListBox ItemsSource="{Binding Fields}" bi:DragSource.IsEnabled="True" bi:DragSource.AllowedEffects="Copy" />

<!-- Drops are decided by an IDropHandler (usually the view-model); an insertion line shows where the item goes -->
<ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Columns}" bi:DropTarget.Handler="{Binding}" bi:DropTarget.Key="Columns" />

public sealed class MyViewModel : IDropHandler
{
    public DragDropEffects DragOver(DropInfo drop) => drop.Item is Field ? DragDropEffects.Copy : DragDropEffects.None;
    public void Drop(DropInfo drop) => Columns.Insert(drop.Index, ((Field)drop.Item!).ToColumn());
}
  • DropInfo gives the dragged Item, the target's Key (one handler for several targets), the insertion Index among the target's items and the raw Data for drags coming from elsewhere.
  • DropTarget.IsDragOver is true while an accepted drag is over the target (style triggers); DropTarget.Orientation switches the insertion rules to a vertical stack.
  • A handler may explain a refusal (IDropHandler.RefusalReason, optional): the reason is shown under the target and set on it as DropTarget.Refusal while the drag is over it.
  • A scrollable target, or its scroll viewer, scrolls when the pointer nears its edges (AutoScroller, also usable on its own); InsertionIndex holds the pure insertion rules.
  • Style keys DragSource.PreviewStyleKey (a ContentControl; DragSource.PreviewTemplate sets the content), DropTarget.InsertionLineStyleKey (a Border) and DropTarget.RefusalStyleKey (a ContentControl holding the reason).

In the designer, fields are dropped between chips, chips are reordered within a shelf, and dimensions move between Axis and Legend keeping their granularity. A refused field says why (DesignerViewModel.RefusalReason): only measures in Values, only dimensions elsewhere, a field already on the shelf, a full axis, a field of another model.
path: Drag and drop in your controls

items.title: Layout
items.text: The layout says where each visual goes. It is a WPF matter: it lives in the DashboardDocument, next to the report, never in the report itself.

items.title: Bands
items.text:
A dashboard is a stack of bands, each with a mode:

Mode Items Size of an item BandMode.Fit A grid of 12 columns filling the width, in lines ColumnSpan in columns, RowSpan in rows BandMode.Wrap Side by side, breaking lines when the next one does not fit, then sharing what is left on each line At least DashboardPanel.MinItemWidth, or Width in pixels BandMode.Scroll On one line, scrolling sideways when they do not fit The same as Wrap

items.title: Items are greedy
items.text: An item without a size shares the room its neighbours leave: a dashboard never has a gap. An item with a size keeps it, the others take the rest. When every item of a line has a size, the room left is a free space, which the dashboard offers to fill.

items.title: Lines and containers
items.text:
A Fit band is a stack of lines. A line is an item, or a container of items and containers:

  • LayoutNode.Row(...): side by side;
  • LayoutNode.Column(...): stacked.

Along a container, items with a size keep it and the others share the rest; across it, every child takes the whole room. An item with a RowSpan sets the height of its line, and the items next to it stretch.

new DashboardLayoutDefinition
{
    Bands =
    [
        new BandLayout
        {
            Items =
            [
                new LayoutNode { VisualId = title.Id, RowSpan = 1 },                         // (1)!
                LayoutNode.Row(
                    new LayoutNode { VisualId = map.Id, ColumnSpan = 6, RowSpan = 6 },        // (2)!
                    LayoutNode.Column(LayoutNode.Item(sales.Id), LayoutNode.Item(margin.Id))), // (3)!
            ],
        },
        new BandLayout
        {
            Mode = BandMode.Scroll,
            Items = [LayoutNode.Item(a.Id), new LayoutNode { VisualId = b.Id, Width = 360 }],
        },
    ],
};
  1. A whole line, one row high.
  2. The left half, six rows high.
  3. Two items stacked beside it, sharing its height.
DashboardLayoutDefinition Default Columns 12 RowHeight 110 pixels

items.title: Narrow screens
items.text:
On a narrow dashboard, Fit bands show fewer columns: one under 600 pixels, six under 960 (ColumnTier.Defaults, set with DashboardPanel.ColumnTiers).

Spans are scaled to the tier, and a line whose items would get less than 3 columns each is broken into several lines. Only the display adapts: the saved layout does not change, and a resize made on a narrow screen is saved in the layout's columns.

items.title: Change it from code
items.text:
DashboardView has methods that keep the layout consistent and make one undo step each: AddNextTo, AddIn (a free space), InsertLine, SetAutoSize, SetVisual, InsertBand, RemoveBand, SetBandMode. Group several into one step with BeginEdit:

using (var edit = dashboard.BeginEdit())
{
    var item = dashboard.AddNextTo(anchor, ItemSide.Right);
    dashboard.SetVisual(item, visual);
    edit.Commit();
}
Lower levels
  • DashboardLayout (static) changes the layout of any DashboardPanel: AddNextTo, MoveNextTo, InsertAt, MoveTo, Resize, ResizeWidth, SetAuto, Remove, InsertBand, RemoveBand, SetBandMode, Update, Capture, GetLayout, SetLayout.
  • DashboardLayoutEngine holds the rules as pure functions on the records, usable without any UI.
  • DashboardPanel shows a layout on its own (Layout, children matched by DashboardPanel.ItemId), and exposes hit tests for interactions: EdgeAt, FlowIndexAt, FreeSpaces, CaptureGeometry. The geometry is a pure function, BandArrangement.Arrange.

items.title: What users do
items.text: Everything on this page works out of the box, and each interaction is a behavior you can configure, replace or remove. Every action is one undo step.

items.title: Make visuals from fields
items.text:
Drag a field from the field list onto the dashboard: next to an item, between two lines, or onto a free space. It makes a visual; the other items make room live around a placeholder.

Dropped Gives A measure, where an item can go A KPI of that measure A dimension, where an item can go The first measure by that dimension: a line by month for a date, bars otherwise Onto an empty item Fills it Onto a visual Adds the field to it: a measure to its values, a dimension to its axis, then its legend; a dimension breaks a KPI down into bars Change what a field makes

The rules are pure functions in FieldVisuals (Create, AddField). Set FieldDropBehavior.CreateVisual and AddField to replace them.

items.title: Add an item
items.text:
• "+" on the right and bottom edges of an item adds an item next to it; "+" between lines and between bands adds a line or a band.
  • A free space (room left by items of fixed size) shows a placeholder that adds an item there.
  • An empty item offers a visual (opens the designer), a text or an image.

items.title: Move
items.text: Drag an item by its grip (⠿, top left on hover). Near an item's edge it goes next to it, between two lines it becomes a line of its own, over a free space it fills it. The other items make room live; Escape cancels.

items.title: Resize
items.text:
Drag the handle in an item's bottom right corner. In a grid band, the item snaps to columns and rows; elsewhere, it takes a width in pixels. Its neighbours share the rest; when they all have a fixed size, the room left becomes a free space.

The toolbar's ↔ button gives a resized item its automatic size back.

items.title: The item toolbar
items.text:
On hover or selection, an item shows its toolbar:

Item Buttons Any ↔ automatic size (once resized), ✎ edit, ✕ remove Text Size, bold, alignment; double-click edits the text in place Image Fit: contain, cover, stretch

✎ on a visual opens the designer in a dialog.

items.title: Select
items.text: Action Result Click an item Selects it Ctrl + click Adds or removes it (on a chart's bar, slice or row, extends the cross-filtering instead) Drag from the background Draws a selection box Click the background, Esc Unselects Ctrl+A Selects everything

items.title: Keyboard
items.text: Keys Action Arrows Select the nearest item in that direction (Shift adds it) Ctrl + arrows Move the selected item: Left/Right swap it with its neighbour, Down/Up move it to the next line or band Ctrl+Shift+Down / Ctrl+Shift+Up Move it to a new band below / above Alt + arrows Extend the selected items over the free room next to them Del Remove the selection Ctrl+D Duplicate the selection Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V Copy, cut, paste Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y Undo, redo

items.title: Copy and paste
items.text:
Copied items keep their arrangement and sizes, and paste after the line of the last selected item, also into another dashboard. They take along the calculated measures they use; a measure whose name is taken by another definition is renamed. Visuals of a model the target does not know are left out.

The clipboard

The clipboard holds an easybi/v1 report with the visuals and their calculated measures (VisualTransfer.ClipboardFormat), their titles as text, and their layout (DashboardView.LayoutClipboardFormat). CreateCopy and Paste(data) work without the clipboard.

items.title: Bands
items.text: The ⋮ menu on the left of a band changes its mode (Fit, Scroll, Wrap: see Layout), inserts a band or removes it. Shift + wheel, or the scroll bar, scrolls a Scroll band.

items.title: Calculated measures
items.text: Ratios, shares, conditional sums: measures computed from the rows of each group, inside the same query. You declare some in the model; your users write their own in a formula editor.

items.title: Why not just a measure?
items.text: A ratio cannot be summed: the margin rate of a region is its total margin divided by its total revenue, not the average of its sales' rates. A calculated measure is computed per group, in the query (in SQL with EF Core), so it can be sorted, limited to a Top N and filtered like the others. Users cannot change its aggregation.

items.title: Declared by you
items.text:
Method For Ratio A sum divided by a sum; empty when the denominator sums to zero Calculated Any aggregate expression over the rows of the group Formula A formula, as users write them: they can read and rewrite it 
model
    .Ratio(s => s.Margin, s => s.Amount, "Margin rate", "MarginRate", format: "P1")      // Σ margin / Σ revenue
    .Ratio(s => s.Amount, s => 1, "Average basket", "AverageBasket", format: "#,##0 €")   // Σ revenue / number of sales
    .Calculated(g => g.Sum(s => s.Amount) - g.Sum(s => s.Cost), "Gross profit", "GrossProfit")
    .Formula("SUM([Amount]; [Channel] = \"Web\") / [Amount]", "Web share", "WebShare", format: "P1");

Guard your divisions

With Calculated, guard divisions yourself: some databases fail on a division by zero. Ratio and formulas do it for you. A Formula may only use fields declared before it; an invalid one throws an ArgumentException.

items.title: Created by your users
items.text:
In the field list, + Calculated measure opens the editor; ✎ and ✕ on a measure's hover edit and delete it. Users give a name, a format and a formula over the model's fields, written with their captions.

The editor helps them as they type:

  • the formula is colored, and its problem underlined and explained;
  • the help of the function the caret is in shows above it;
  • suggestions only offer what can be written there: after SUM(, measures and number dimensions; in a condition, dimensions; after [Region] =, the values of Region; after a condition, AND and OR;
  • operators come as a keypad, functions, measures and dimensions in tabs to search and insert;
  • the measure's total previews as it is typed.

items.title: The formula language
items.text: Formula Computes [Margin] / [Revenue] The margin rate of each group SUM([Quantity] * [Unit price]) A sum of a product, row by row SUM([Revenue]; [Region] = "North") / [Revenue] The share of the North COUNT([Channel] = "Web" AND [Date] >= "2024-01-01") The rows matching a condition DISTINCTCOUNT([Customer]) The number of distinct customers IF([Revenue] > 1000; [Margin]; 0) A value by condition

items.title: Functions
items.text:
Function SUM, AVERAGE (or AVG), MIN, MAX Aggregate an expression read row by row. An optional last argument keeps the rows matching a condition. COUNT(), COUNT(condition) The rows, or those matching the condition. DISTINCTCOUNT(field) The distinct non-empty values. IF(condition; then; else) On the group or on each row; without else, empty.

A measure on its own ([Revenue]) is aggregated as in the field list. MeasureFormula.Functions lists the functions with their usage and description, in the user's language.

items.title: Syntax
items.text:
• Operators: + - * / and parentheses. A division by zero gives an empty value.
  • Comparisons: = <> < <= > >= (texts and yes/no values with = and <> only), combined with AND, OR, NOT; TRUE and FALSE.
  • Numbers take a decimal point; texts and dates go in double quotes: "North", "2024-12-31".
  • Arguments are separated by ; or ,.
  • A dimension is only used inside a function; a measure calculated by the model (Ratio, Calculated) only outside.

In SQL, formulas become CASE WHEN, COUNT(DISTINCT ...)... in the same query as the other measures.

items.title: Measures using measures
items.text:
A formula can use the report's other calculated measures: with [Cost] = [Revenue] - [Margin], the cost rate is [Cost] / [Revenue]. They are computed per group, so they are used on their own, not inside a function.

  • A measure cannot use itself, even through others: A measure cannot use itself: this measure → [Cost] → this measure. This is checked as it is typed and when a report is opened.
  • Deleting a measure names the measures that use it.
  • A copied visual takes the measures it uses along; pasted formulas follow the measures that are renamed.

items.title: Redefining a model's measure
items.text:
Users can also change the measures you declared (✎ on any measure). Their version is saved in the report under the same name, and redefines the measure for the whole report:

  • a formula that is only the measure itself ([Revenue]) keeps your computation, and only changes its caption and format;
  • any other formula replaces the computation: AVERAGE([Revenue]) changes the aggregation, the measure's name in it still meaning your definition.

↺ in the field list, or Restore in the editor, removes the redefinition.

items.title: Where they are saved
items.text:
Calculated measures live in EasyBIContext.Measures, one per open report: every field list, designer and visual of the context sees them.

With a dashboardWithout a dashboard

The DashboardView loads and saves them with its document. Undo does not remove them.

report = report with { Measures = context.Measures.Measures.ToArray() };   // save
context.Measures.Load(report.Measures);                                     // open
Your own formula editor

FormulaEditing (Tokenize, Calls, CallAt, CompletionAt, ContextAt) and MeasureFormula.Check (the problem and where it is written) give the same help as EasyBI's editor. CalculatedMeasureEditor exposes it as a view-model: Tabs, Search, OperatorGroups, Suggest, Accept, Insert, CurrentCall, Problem. MeasureContext gives MeasuresOf, GetField, Definition, Needed, UsedBy, Using; MeasureFormula Validate, Check, ToDisplay and Rename.

items.title: Cross-filtering
items.text:
A click on a bar, a point, a slice or a row filters the other visuals of the dashboard on what it shows. Below, the Île-de-France / Partenaires bar is clicked: its visual dims the rest and shows the selection, and the revenue by quarter now counts those sales only.

It works as soon as the visuals share a FilterContext, as for global filters.

items.title: What users do
items.text:
Action Result Click an element It becomes the selection: the other visuals keep its rows. Click it again Clears the selection. Ctrl + click in the same visual Adds the element to the selection, or removes it: Region = Nord or Sud. Ctrl + click in another visual Adds that visual's selection: (Region = Nord or Sud) and Channel = Web. Click the ✕ of a selection Clears that visual's selection. Click the ✕ of the filter bar's summary Clears every selection.

An element filters on the dimensions it shows: its category (every axis field), and its series for a chart with a legend. A clicked period (a quarter, a month) filters on that period.

A visual is not filtered by its own selection

It keeps showing everything, dims what is left out, and shows a summary of its selection.

items.title: In code
items.text:
Filters.Selections;                       // one CrossFilter per visual with a selection
Filters.SelectionOf(visual.Id);
Filters.ClearSelection(visual.Id);
Filters.ClearSelection();                 // all of them
Filters.DescribeSelections(name => context.GetModel(name).Metadata);

Selections are not saved with the report: they are the state of a session.

items.title: In a connector
items.text:
A connector reports clicks and draws the selection; EasyBI does the rest.

// On click (Select is null when the visual is not interactive, as in the designer's preview)
request.Select?.Invoke(new CategorySelection(category, series));

// When drawing: the elements outside the selection are dimmed
var opacity = request.IsEmphasized(category, series) ? 1 : SelectionFilters.DimmedOpacity;

Tables report a RowSelection and use IsRowEmphasized(row). See Writing a connector.

items.title: Filters
items.text:
Filters keep the rows that matter: the last 12 months, three regions, the sales over 1,000 €. They run inside the query, in the database.

Filter Set by Applies to Global filter The filter bar Every visual of its model Visual filter The designer's Filters well Its visual Selection A click on a chart The other visuals: see Cross-filtering

items.title: The filter bar
items.text:
A FilterContext holds the filters of a dashboard. Set it once on a container (it is inherited): the filter bar edits it, and every VisualView inside applies it.

<DockPanel bi:VisualView.FilterContext="{Binding Filters}"> <!-- (1)! -->
    <bi:FilterBar DockPanel.Dock="Top" Context="{Binding Context}" />
    <bi:DashboardView Context="{Binding Context}" />
</DockPanel>
  1. public FilterContext Filters { get; } = new(); in your view-model.

Global filters are saved with the report, in ReportDefinition.Filters:

var report = dashboard.Capture().Report with { Filters = Filters.Filters.ToArray() };   // save
Filters.Load(report.Filters);                                                           // open

items.title: Values
items.text:
Any dimension can be filtered on a list of values, checked in a list that users can search.

new FilterSpec("Region", FilterOperator.In, ["Nord", "Sud"])
new FilterSpec("Channel", FilterOperator.NotIn, ["Web"])

items.title: Periods
items.text:
A date is filtered on a period rather than a list of values:

Period FilterSpec Between two dates (an end may stay open) PeriodFilters.Between("Date", new DateOnly(2024, 1, 1), null) The current day, month, quarter or year PeriodFilters.Relative("Date", FilterOperator.Current, DateGrain.Year) The last n, the current one included (last 12 months) PeriodFilters.Relative("Date", FilterOperator.Last, DateGrain.Month, 12) The n previous complete ones (last month) PeriodFilters.Relative("Date", FilterOperator.Previous, DateGrain.Month)

Relative periods are resolved when the query runs: a saved report keeps showing the last 12 months. The date is compared with the period's bounds (date >= start AND date < end), so the database can use an index on it.

items.title: Numbers
items.text:
A number dimension is filtered on values, or compared with numbers:

NumericFilters.Range("Quantity", 10, null);                                   // Quantity >= 10
NumericFilters.Compare("Quantity", FilterOperator.LessThan, 5);               // Quantity < 5

Operators: GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual, Range (inclusive, an end may stay open).

items.title: Measures
items.text:
A measure dropped on the designer's Filters well filters the visual's groups by their total: regions whose revenue ≥ 10,000. The comparison runs after the grouping (a SQL HAVING), before the sort and Top N.

Filters = [NumericFilters.Compare("Amount", FilterOperator.GreaterThanOrEqual, 10_000)],

Only in a visual

The meaning of a measure filter depends on the visual's grouping, so the filter bar does not offer measures.

items.title: Describe a filter
items.text: PeriodFilters.Describe(filter) and NumericFilters.Describe(filter) give the text the filter bar shows, in the user's language: Last 12 months, ≥ 10,000.

items.title: Semantic model
items.text:
The semantic model is what you, the developer, declare: which fields of your data users can analyze, under which names. Users never see your classes or your tables, only the model.

SemanticModel.For(sales, "sales", "Sales")
  .Dimension(s => s.Date, "Date")
  .Dimension(s => s.Region, "Region")
  .Dimension(s => s.Channel, "Channel")
  .Dimension(s => s.Product.Category,
             "Category")
  .Dimension(s => s.Product.Name,
             "Product")
  .Measure(s => s.Amount, "Revenue",
           format: "#,##0 €")
  .Measure(s => s.Margin, "Margin",
           format: "#,##0 €")
  .Measure(s => s.Quantity, "Quantity")
  .Count("Number of sales")
  .Ratio(s => s.Margin, s => s.Amount,
         "Margin rate", "MarginRate",
         format: "P1");

items.title: Dimensions
items.text:
A dimension is what users group or filter by: a region, a channel, a date, a product category.

.Dimension(s => s.Region, "Region")
.Dimension(s => s.Product.Category, "Category")          // (1)!
.Dimension(s => s.Customer.Country, "Country", name: "Country") // (2)!
  1. Navigation properties work: with EF Core, they become joins in SQL.
  2. The name is the member path by default (Customer.Country); give your own to keep reports stable when the class changes.

What users can do with a dimension depends on its type:

Type Examples Users can Text string, enum Group, filter on values, search Number int, decimal, double Group, filter on values or ranges (≥, <, between) Date DateTime, DateOnly, DateTimeOffset Group by year, quarter, month or day; filter on periods (this year, last 12 months, between) Boolean bool Group, filter on yes / no

items.title: Measures
items.text:
A measure is what users add up: a revenue, a quantity, a number of sales.

.Measure(s => s.Amount, "Revenue", format: "#,##0 €")              // summed by default
.Measure(s => s.UnitPrice, "Unit price", Aggregation.Average, "C2") // (1)!
.Count("Number of sales")                                          // (2)!
  1. The default aggregation; users can switch to Sum, Average, Min, Max or Count in the designer.
  2. Counts rows. Its name is Count unless you give another.

Formats are .NET format strings, applied in the user's culture: N0 (12,345), #,##0 € (12,345 €), C2 (currency of the culture), P1 (12.3%). Users can override them per visual, with conditional formatting too.

items.title: Calculated measures
items.text:
A ratio cannot be summed: the margin rate of a region is its total margin divided by its total revenue, not the average of its sales' rates. Calculated measures are computed per group, inside the query:

Method For Example Ratio A sum divided by a sum Margin rate, average basket Calculated Any aggregate expression g => g.Sum(s => s.Amount) - g.Sum(s => s.Cost) Formula A formula users can read and rewrite SUM([Amount]; [Channel] = "Web") / [Amount]

Users create their own too. See Calculated measures.

items.title: Names and captions
items.text:
Every model and field has two labels:

Seen by Example Must Name Reports (JSON), your code sales, Amount, Product.Category Stay stable: saved reports refer to it Caption Users Sales, Revenue, Category Read well; can follow the language

Renaming a property breaks saved reports

A field's name defaults to its member path. Before renaming a property of your class, give the field its old name explicitly (name: "Amount"), or saved reports will show the field as missing (EasyBIContext.Validate lists such problems).

Captions can follow the user's language: call .Localize(MyStrings.ResourceManager) and every caption becomes a resource key. See Localization.

items.title: Data sources
items.text:
In memoryEF Core (recommended)Shared IQueryable 
SemanticModel.For(sales, "sales", "Sales")   // any IEnumerable<T>

Queries run in LINQ to objects, in parallel.

SemanticModel.For(() => dbFactory.CreateDbContext(), db => db.Sales, "sales", "Sales")

Each query opens its own DbContext (from an IDbContextFactory) and disposes it: the visuals of a dashboard query in parallel.

SemanticModel.For(dbContext.Sales, "sales", "Sales")

One DbContext for every query: they run one after another, since a DbContext does not support concurrent operations.

Every visual becomes one query, with its filters, grouping, aggregates, sort and Top N inside the IQueryable. With EF Core, that is one SQL statement: only the aggregated rows reach the application, whatever the size of the table.

The SQL of a visual

Revenue by region, top 3, on SQL Server, is roughly:

SELECT TOP(3) [s].[Region], SUM([s].[Amount])
FROM [Sales] AS [s]
GROUP BY [s].[Region]
ORDER BY SUM([s].[Amount]) DESC

Keep dimension and measure expressions translatable by your provider: a method call EF Core cannot translate fails when the visual queries.

items.title: Several models
items.text:
Add as many models as you need; the designer lets users pick one, and each visual uses a single model.

EasyBIContext.Create()
    .AddModel(salesModel)
    .AddModel(stockModel)
    .UseRenderer(new LiveCharts2Renderer());

items.title: When the data changes
items.text:
Visuals cache their last result and query again only when their own query changes. When the rows change (an import, another data source), tell them, from any thread:

context.RefreshData("sales");   // the visuals of this model
context.RefreshData();          // every visual

items.title: When a query fails
items.text:
A visual whose query throws (a database out of reach, an expression EF Core cannot translate) or whose renderer throws does not show the exception: it says it could not be displayed, with Retry, which runs the query again, and See what happened.

The details tell what failed (the query or the renderer) and give the visual, the version of EasyBI and the exception with its stack trace, ready to copy into a bug report.

EasyBIContext.VisualFailed tells the application first: log the failure, say what happened in the user's words, or keep the details from the user.

context.VisualFailed += (_, e) =>
{
    logger.LogError(e.Exception, "Visual {Title} failed ({Stage})", e.Visual.Title, e.Stage);
    if (e.Exception is TimeoutException) e.Message = "The sales database is not answering. Try again in a moment.";
    e.ShowDetails = false;   // no technical details in production
};

e.Stage is Query or Render (with e.Renderer), and e.Details is the text the details show. The sample shows it with its Unavailable source data source.

items.title: Your own model
items.text: SemanticModel.For covers any IQueryable. For another kind of source (a web API, an OLAP cube...), implement ISemanticModel: its Metadata (the fields), ExecuteAsync (an AnalyticQuery in, a ResultSet out) and GetDistinctValuesAsync (the values filters offer).

items.title: The designer
items.text:
The ReportDesigner lets end users build a visual by themselves: they drag fields onto wells, pick a visual type and see the result live.

Zone What the end user does there 1 Fields Picks the model, searches a field, drags it (or double-clicks it). Creates calculated measures. 2 Header Folds the field panel, undoes and redoes, names the visual, opens the gallery of types, folds the properties panel. 3 Wells Drops fields: axis, legend, values, tooltip, filters. Their names and limits follow the type. 4 Preview Sees the visual as it will show, with the real data. 5 Properties Sets the selected chip (aggregation, grain, format...), or the visual when no chip is selected.

items.title: Show it
items.text:
The designer needs an EasyBIContext (your models and renderers). Bind the visual being designed to keep what the end user builds: Visual is two-way.

XAMLCode-behind 
<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}"
                   Visual="{Binding EditedVisual}" /> <!-- (1)! -->
  1. Two-way by default: every change of the end user comes back into EditedVisual.
designer.Context = context;
designer.Visual = visual;            // (1)!
// ...
var designed = designer.Visual;      // (2)!
  1. Loads the visual, with a new history of changes. null starts a new visual.
  2. What the end user built, after every change.

No view-model is needed. The sample's XAML only tab shows a designer declared without any code.

Show the result elsewhere

Visual is a plain VisualDefinition: bind it to a VisualView to show the visual being designed somewhere else, or save it as JSON.

<bi:VisualView Context="{Binding Context}" Definition="{Binding Visual, ElementName=Designer}" />

items.title: Save what the end user built
items.text:
Visual is ready to store: add it to a ReportDefinition, or serialize it on its own.

if (VisualValidator.Validate(designer.Visual!, context.VisualTypes) is { } problem)
{
    MessageBox.Show(problem);            // (1)!
    return;
}
report = report with { Visuals = [.. report.Visuals, designer.Visual!] };
designer.Visual = null;                  // (2)!
  1. A visual can be incomplete while it is designed: a pie without a category, a chart without a value...
  2. Starts the next visual.

items.title: Drive it from your buttons
items.text:
Undo and Redo are WPF commands of the control: point a button at it.

<Button Content="Undo" Command="Undo" CommandTarget="{Binding ElementName=Designer}" />
<Button Content="Redo" Command="Redo" CommandTarget="{Binding ElementName=Designer}" />
Property Context The models and renderers the designer offers. Changing it starts a new designer state. Visual The visual being designed (two-way). null: a new visual. Rules What the end user may change: see Rules. IsFieldPanelOpen, IsPropertiesPanelOpen Whether the side panels are shown (two-way). Selecting a chip opens the properties. ViewModel The designer's state (DesignerViewModel, read-only): selection, undo history, properties panel. The view-model, for advanced use

The control creates a DesignerViewModel for its Context and gives it to its template as data context, so the content of its slots binds to it too. Reach it through designer.ViewModel for what the control does not expose: SelectedItem, CanUndo, Refusal, PropertiesBuilding...

items.title: Next
items.text:
• Building a visual

    What end users do: the gallery, the wells, the chips, the keyboard.

  • Rules

    Lock the type, the fields, or anything of the visual.

  • Customizing

    Your own buttons, properties, editors and icons.

items.title: Building a visual
items.text: What the end user does in the designer, step by step. Everything here works out of the box: this page is also a base for your application's user help.

items.title: Add fields
items.text:
Drag a field from the list onto a well, or double-click it: a dimension goes to the axis, a measure to the values.

While a field is dragged, the wells tell whether they take it. Below, Channel (a dimension) is dragged over a bar chart: the axis, the legend and the filters take it, the values do not.

A well that refuses a field says why, in the end user's language:

Refusal When Only measures go in Values A dimension dropped on the values. Only dimensions go in Axis A measure dropped on the axis or the legend. Region is already in Axis The field is already there. Category holds a single field The type allows one field there (a pie's category). Axis is not used by this type of visual A KPI has no axis, for instance. Region belongs to the model "Sales": choose this model first The field is from another model.

items.title: Pick a visual type
items.text:
The type button opens a gallery grouped by use. A type that the active renderer cannot draw is greyed.

The wells follow the type: their names and limits change, and the wells a type does not use disappear.

Type Wells Bars, stacked bars, points, lines, areas Axis (up to 3 fields), Legend, Values, Tooltip, Filters Pie, donut Category (1), Value (1), Tooltip, Filters Waterfall Axis (1 to 3), Value (1), Tooltip, Filters KPI Values, Filters Gauge Value (1), Filters Table Rows (up to 3), Values, Filters Matrix Rows (up to 4), Columns (1), Values, Filters

Nothing is lost when the type changes

A well the new type does not use keeps its fields and stays shown, marked Not used by this type of visual, until the end user removes them or picks a type that uses them again.

items.title: Arrange the chips
items.text:
A field in a well is a chip. Its badges sum its settings up: Σ or avg (aggregation), Quarter (grain), PY (time comparison), Y2 (secondary axis), ↓ (sort).

  • Move a chip by dragging it, within its well (the order of the axis or of the series) or to another well.
  • Remove it with its ×, or with Del once selected.
  • Select it with a click: the properties panel shows its settings.

items.title: Set the details
items.text:
The properties panel shows the settings of the selected chip, in sections:

Selection Sections A measure Aggregation, time comparison, chart type and secondary axis, sort, formatting A dimension Grain (dates), sort, value labels A filter Its values, or a period for a date Nothing (Escape) Title, sort, Top N, legend, tooltips, the renderer's options

items.title: Undo, redo, keyboard
items.text:
Every change of the visual can be undone: Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z), or the header's arrows. The history keeps 100 steps and starts over when another visual is loaded.

Once a chip is selected, the keyboard drives the wells:

Keys Action Left / Right Previous / next chip Up / Down Chip of the well above / below Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right Move the selected chip within its well Del Remove the selected chip Esc Select the visual (its settings show)

Text boxes and lists keep their own keys: typing a title never moves a chip.

items.title: Customizing the designer
items.text:
Every part of the designer can be changed without rewriting it: add your buttons, hide a part, add your own settings to the properties panel, restyle an editor, draw your own icons.

To... Use Add your own buttons A slot Hide a part A slot in Hide mode Add settings to the properties panel PropertiesBuilding Restyle an editor of the panel A DataTemplate with a DesignerPropertyTemplates key Change the icon of a type A Geometry with a VisualTypeIconKey Fold the side panels IsFieldPanelOpen, IsPropertiesPanelOpen

items.title: Add your own buttons
items.text:
The designer is made of named slots: put your content before, after or instead of each one. The sample puts its New visual and Add to dashboard buttons under the preview:

<bi:ReportDesigner x:Name="Designer" Context="{Binding Context}">
    <bi:Slots.Items>
        <bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.Preview}"> <!-- (1)! -->
            <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" HorizontalAlignment="Right" Margin="0,10,0,0">
                <Button Content="New visual" Click="OnNewVisual" />
                <Button Content="Add to dashboard" Click="OnPublish" Margin="6,0,0,0" />
            </StackPanel>
        </bi:Slot>
    </bi:Slots.Items>
</bi:ReportDesigner>
  1. Mode="After" by default: below the preview, since this slot is vertical. Before, Replace and Hide are the other modes.

The slots of the designer:

FieldPanel ─ Fields               Header ─ Title, VisualTypes          Properties
                                  Shelves ─ AxisShelf, LegendShelf,
                                            ValuesShelf, TooltipShelf,
                                            FiltersShelf
                                  Preview

Data context of a slot

The content of a designer slot takes the designer's ViewModel as data context: {Binding Visual.Title} works in it. To bind to your window's view-model, go through the window: {Binding DataContext.PublishCommand, RelativeSource={RelativeSource AncestorType=Window}}.

See Slots for the modes, inheritance and templates.

items.title: Hide a part
items.text:
<bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.FiltersShelf}" Mode="Hide" />
<bi:Slot Name="{x:Static bi:ReportDesignerSlots.TooltipShelf}" Mode="Hide" />

Slots.Hide(designer, ReportDesignerSlots.VisualTypes);   // no type button

Hiding a part does not forbid what it does: to forbid a change, add a rule.

items.title: Add settings to the properties panel
items.text:
The panel is rebuilt from sections of properties each time the selection changes. PropertiesBuilding lets you add, remove or reorder them. Here, a Notes section for the measures:

designer.ViewModel!.PropertiesBuilding += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Selection is ShelfItemViewModel { IsValue: true } chip)
        e.Sections.Insert(0, new DesignerPropertySection(
            "Notes", () => "Notes",
            [
                DesignerProperty.Text(
                    "Comment", () => "Comment",
                    get: () => comments.Get(chip.Field.Name),
                    set: text => comments.Set(chip.Field.Name, text)),
            ]));
};

e.Selection Selected ShelfItemViewModel A chip of the axis, legend, values or tooltip (IsValue: a measure in the values) FilterItemViewModel A chip of the filters null Nothing: the visual's settings

Properties come in six kinds, each with its editor:

Factory Editor DesignerProperty.Toggle Check box DesignerProperty.Choice Drop-down list of Option<T> DesignerProperty.Number Number box (empty = null) DesignerProperty.Text Text box DesignerProperty.Info Read-only text DesignerProperty.Custom Any object, shown with its DataTemplate

Labels are functions (() => "Notes") so that they follow a change of language: return a localized string. Each factory also takes isAvailable (to grey the property) and description (its tooltip).

EasyBI's sections have constant keys, to find or remove them:

var tooltips = e.Sections.FirstOrDefault(s => s.Key == DesignerPropertySections.Tooltips);
if (tooltips is not null) e.Sections.Remove(tooltips);

Field, Formatting, Filter, ValueLabels, Visual, Tooltips, Options (the renderer's options).

items.title: Restyle an editor of the panel
items.text:
Each kind of property is drawn by a DataTemplate whose data context is the DesignerProperty. Define one with the same key in your resources to replace EasyBI's:

<DataTemplate x:Key="{x:Static bi:DesignerPropertyTemplates.ToggleTemplateKey}">
    <ToggleButton Content="{Binding Label}" IsChecked="{Binding IsOn}" Style="{StaticResource MySwitch}" />
</DataTemplate>
Key Binds to ToggleTemplateKey Label, IsOn ChoiceTemplateKey Choices (with Label), SelectedChoice NumberTemplateKey NumberText TextTemplateKey TextValue InfoTemplateKey TextValue CustomTemplateKey Value

items.title: Change the icon of a type
items.text:
The icons of the gallery are geometries drawn with the foreground in a 16×16 box. Define one with the type's key, for your own types or to replace one of EasyBI's:

<Application.Resources>
    <Geometry x:Key="{bi:VisualTypeIconKey sample.ranking}">
        M1.5,3 L3,3 M1.5,8 L3,8 M1.5,13 L3,13 M5,3 L14.5,3 M5,8 L11,8 M5,13 L8,13
    </Geometry>
    <Geometry x:Key="{bi:VisualTypeIconKey Bar}">M2,14 L2,6 L6,6 L6,14 Z M10,14 L10,2 L14,2 L14,14 Z</Geometry>
</Application.Resources>

A type without an icon shows the one under VisualTypeIcons.DefaultKey.

items.title: Fold the side panels
items.text:
Both side panels fold, from the header's buttons or from your code. Both properties are two-way:

<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}"
                   IsFieldPanelOpen="{Binding ShowFields}"
                   IsPropertiesPanelOpen="False" />

Selecting a chip opens the properties panel, so that its settings show.

items.title: Rules
items.text: Rules decide what the end user may change in the visual: keep its type, its fields, a maximum of measures, or anything else. A refused change does not happen, and the designer says why.

items.title: Ready-made rules
items.text:
Three rules come with EasyBI, declared as behaviors of the designer:

<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}">
    <i:Interaction.Behaviors> <!-- (1)! -->
        <bi:LockVisualTypeBehavior />
    </i:Interaction.Behaviors>
</bi:ReportDesigner>
  1. xmlns:i="http://schemas.microsoft.com/xaml/behaviors"
Behavior Refuses Still allowed LockVisualTypeBehavior Another visual type Everything else LockFieldsBehavior Adding, removing or moving a field, in any well The settings of the fields: aggregation, format, grain, filter values... and the title ReadOnlyDesignerBehavior Any change Selecting chips to read their settings

Each takes an optional Message, shown instead of EasyBI's (translated) one: <bi:LockFieldsBehavior Message="Ask your administrator to change the fields" />.

items.title: Your own rules
items.text:
A rule is a function: it receives the change and returns null to accept it, or the message of the refusal.

designer.Rules.Add(change =>
    change.After.Values.Count > 3 ? "Three measures at most" : null);

The change is a VisualChange, the visual Before and After it:

Member Use Before, After The whole visuals (VisualDefinition): look at anything. Changes(v => ...) Whether a part differs, compared by value: change.Changes(v => v.Type), change.Changes(v => v.Filters). FieldsChanged Whether a field was added, removed or moved, in any well (not its settings).

The first rule that refuses wins. The rules stay when the designer's Context changes.

items.title: Declare it in XAML
items.text:
Derive from DesignerRuleBehavior to declare a rule in XAML, like the ready-made ones:

XAMLC# 
<bi:ReportDesigner Context="{Binding Context}">
    <i:Interaction.Behaviors>
        <local:MaxMeasuresBehavior Max="3" />
    </i:Interaction.Behaviors>
</bi:ReportDesigner>

public sealed class MaxMeasuresBehavior : DesignerRuleBehavior
{
    public int Max { get; set; } = 3;

    protected override string? Check(VisualChange change) =>
        change.After.Values.Count > Max ? Message ?? $"{Max} measures at most" : null;
}

items.title: Recipes
What the end user sees
items.text:
What a rule would refuse is shown before the end user tries it:

  • The gallery greys the refused types; the message is their tooltip.
  • A well refuses a dragged field it would not accept, with the message.
  • A chip loses its × when removing it is refused.
  • A text or a number typed in the properties panel is checked once entered: refused, it comes back to its value, and the message shows above the wells.

Keep rules quick and without side effects

To grey what it would refuse, the designer calls each rule with candidate changes: one per type of the gallery, one per well when a drag starts... A rule must not change anything, nor take time (no database call).

What does not go through the rules

Setting Visual (loading a visual, or null), undo and redo. The rules judge the end user's changes, not the application's.

items.title: Rules or slots?
items.text: A rule forbids a change whatever the way the end user makes it, including the ways future versions of the designer will add. A slot only hides a part of the designer. Both go well together: hide the type button to keep the header simple, and lock the type with a rule to be sure.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• A filter on a measure compares the measure as the model aggregates it, whatever aggregation the visual shows.
  • Relative periods ("last 12 months") are resolved in the local time zone when a visual queries; an open dashboard does not query again at midnight.
  • Top applies to aggregated rows, not to categories when a legend is present.
  • Grouping, sorting and Top are pushed down to the provider, and execution is asynchronous when the source implements IAsyncEnumerable (EF Core). The SQL translation was checked manually with EF Core 8 on SQLite (every query shape, including date granularities, navigation properties and sort on an aggregate); there is no automated test against a database. SQLite cannot sum decimal columns (EF Core refuses the query).
  • At most 4 grouping dimensions (axis + legend).
  • The built-in light and dark themes do not restyle standard controls (buttons, combo boxes...): use a control library for those (see Following a control library).
  • EasyBI.Themes.WpfUi is checked against WPF UI's light and dark themes; its high contrast themes are not verified.
  • Dashboard images are embedded in the file (2 MB by default, DashboardView.MaxImageBytes).

items.title: Report format (easybi/v1)
items.text:
{
  "schema": "easybi/v1",
  "title": "Dashboard",
  "visuals": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue by region and channel",
      "model": "sales",
      "type": "Bar",
      "axis": [ { "field": "Region", "grain": "None", "labels": { "Île-de-France": "IDF" } } ],
      "legend": { "field": "Channel", "grain": "None" },
      "legendPosition": "Bottom",
      "values": [ { "measure": "Amount" }, { "measure": "Count", "seriesType": "Line", "secondaryAxis": true } ],
      "tooltip": { "showPercent": true, "values": [ { "measure": "Quantity" } ], "template": "{category}: {value}" },
      "filters": [
        { "field": "Product.Category", "operator": "In", "values": [ "Services" ] },
        { "field": "Date", "operator": "Last", "values": [ "12" ], "grain": "Month" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "filters": [
    { "model": "sales", "filter": { "field": "Region", "operator": "In", "values": [ "North", null ] } }
  ]
}

A visual's type is the id of its visual type: one of EasyBI's (Bar, StackedBar, Line, Area, Scatter, Pie, Donut, Waterfall, Kpi, Gauge, Table, Matrix, Text, Image, read whatever their case) or one an application declares. A measure's seriesType draws its series with another cartesian type than the visual's.

null in values means a missing value. Besides In and NotIn, a date filter's operator can be Between (values: from and to as yyyy-MM-dd, inclusive, null for an open end), Current, Last or Previous (value: the number of periods; grain is their unit). A number dimension or, in a visual, a measure can be compared: GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual (value: the number, invariant) or Range (values: minimum and maximum, inclusive, null for an open end). An AnyOf filter keeps the rows matching every filter of one of its alternatives (its field and values are empty): cross-filtering builds one when several selected elements differ on more than one dimension, { "field": "", "operator": "AnyOf", "values": [], "alternatives": [[...], [...]] }. EasyBIContext.Validate(report) reports the unknown models and fields of a loaded report, and the formulas that no longer match their model.

Calculated measures created by the end user are saved with the report (the property is omitted when there are none), and visuals reference them by name like a field:

"measures": [
  { "name": "calc_3f9a1c0d2b7e", "caption": "Margin rate", "model": "sales", "formula": "[Margin] / [Amount]", "format": "P1" },
  { "name": "Amount", "caption": "Average revenue", "model": "sales", "formula": "AVERAGE([Amount])", "format": "N0" }
]

A measure named like a measure of its model (the second one) redefines it in the report; an empty caption keeps the model's.

Text and image visuals carry their content and no model:

{ "type": "Text", "text": { "text": "Sales dashboard", "fontSize": 24, "isBold": true, "alignment": "Left" } }
{ "type": "Image", "image": { "data": "iVBORw0KGgo...", "mediaType": "image/png", "fit": "Contain" } }

items.title: Dashboard file (easybi-dashboard/v1)
items.text:
DashboardSerializer saves what a DashboardView shows: the unchanged report next to the WPF layout, which references visuals by id. Sizes that are not saved are greedy. It also opens a plain easybi/v1 report (visuals then get a default layout).

{
  "schema": "easybi-dashboard/v1",
  "report": { "schema": "easybi/v1", "visuals": [ ... ], "filters": [ ... ] },
  "layout": {
    "columns": 12,
    "rowHeight": 110,
    "bands": [
      {
        "mode": "Fit",
        "items": [
          { "visualId": "...", "rowSpan": 1 },
          { "split": "Row", "children": [ { "visualId": "...", "columnSpan": 6 }, { "visualId": "..." } ] }
        ]
      },
      { "mode": "Scroll", "items": [ { "visualId": "...", "width": 360 }, { "visualId": "..." } ] }
    ]
  }
}

The same file renders identically with any connector.

items.title: Visual types
items.text:
A visual is a VisualDefinition: a model, a type, and fields in its wells. Every type below is offered in the designer's gallery and drawn by the connector you plug in (LiveCharts2 or OxyPlot), except the KPI, the gauge, the table, the matrix, the text and the image, which EasyBI draws itself whatever the connector.

new VisualDefinition
{
    Title = "Revenue by region",
    Model = "sales",
    Type = VisualType.Bar,     // (1)!
    Axis = [new("Region")],
    Legend = new("Channel"),   // (2)!
    Values = [new("Amount")],
};
  1. The type: one of the VisualType below, or one of your application's.
  2. Optional: splits the values into one series per channel.

items.title: Comparison
items.text:
• Bars · VisualType.Bar

    Axis (up to 3 fields), Legend, Values. One bar per category and series.

  • Stacked bars · VisualType.StackedBar

    The series of a category piled up: the height is their total.

  • Points · VisualType.Scatter

    A point per category and series, without a line.

items.title: Trend
items.text:
• Lines · VisualType.Line

    Best with a date on the axis: one line per series.

  • Areas · VisualType.Area

    Lines filled down to the axis.

Mix them

The bars, stacked bars, points, lines and areas can be mixed in one chart, one type per measure, with a second value axis: see Combined charts.

items.title: Composition
items.text:
• Pie · VisualType.Pie

    Category (1 field), Value (1 measure).

  • Donut · VisualType.Donut

    A ring with the total in its hole.

  • Waterfall · VisualType.Waterfall

    How each category adds to the running total, up in green, down in red, then the total.

items.title: Indicators and tables
items.text:
• KPI · VisualType.Kpi

    Values only: one big number per measure. Shows ▲ / ▼ for changes over time.

  • Gauge · VisualType.Gauge

    One value on a half circle, with a scale and a target.

  • Table · VisualType.Table

    Rows (up to 3 fields), Values.

  • Matrix · VisualType.Matrix

    Rows crossed with columns, with totals. See Matrix.

items.title: Gauge settings
items.text:
The scale and the target of a gauge are numbers of the visual, edited in the designer's Visual section:

new VisualDefinition
{
    Model = "sales", Type = VisualType.Gauge, Values = [new("MarginRate")],
    Gauge = new GaugeSettings { Minimum = 0, Maximum = 0.5, Target = 0.35 },
};
Setting Empty means Minimum 0 Maximum A round number above 0, the value and the target Target No target mark

The measure's format colors the value and adds its icon.

items.title: Content
items.text:
Texts and images query no model. Users add them to a dashboard and edit them in place.

  • Text · VisualType.Text

    Text = new TextContent
{
    Text = "Sales dashboard",
    FontSize = 24,
    IsBold = true,
    Alignment = TextAlign.Left,
}

  • Image · VisualType.Image

    Embedded in the report, as base64:

    Image = new ImageContent
{
    Data = Convert.ToBase64String(bytes),
    MediaType = "image/png",
    Fit = ImageFit.Contain,
}

items.title: Common settings
items.text:
Property Title Shown above the visual. Sort A field or measure, ascending or descending: Sort = new("Amount", Descending: true). Top Keeps the first N categories after sorting. Filters Filters of this visual only: see Filters. LegendPosition See Legends. Tooltip See Tooltips.

Sort, Top N and filters run inside the query, in the database.

items.title: Several axis fields
items.text:
An axis takes up to three fields: year, then region. The chart draws them as a hierarchy, each outer value once, under its group of bars.

Axis = [new("Date", DateGrain.Year), new("Region")],

How the labels adapt:

  • Each bar is labelled by the innermost field (Nord), each group by the outer one (2024), with a line between the groups.
  • When the bars are too narrow, every n-th group label shows, and the innermost labels give way to the groups'.
  • Sorted on a measure, the categories are no longer grouped: they keep joined labels (2024 / Nord).
  • Tooltips always show the whole category.
For connector authors

CategoryLevels.Of(request.Chart) (EasyBI.Core) gives the short labels and the groups of each outer field (CategoryGroup: label, first category, count, center). LiveCharts2 draws the groups on extra X axes, OxyPlot on axes of the next tiers.

items.title: Combined charts
items.text: Bars, lines, points and areas in one chart: one type per measure, and a second value axis on the right for a measure of another scale.

items.title: In the designer
items.text: Select a measure's chip: its Chart type list overrides the visual's type for that measure, and Secondary axis moves it to the right axis. The chip shows Y2 when it is on the right axis.

items.title: In code
items.text:
new VisualDefinition
{
    Model = "sales",
    Type = VisualType.Bar,                                        // (1)!
    Axis = [new("Date", DateGrain.Quarter)],
    Values =
    [
        new("Amount"),                                            // bars
        new("Margin") { SeriesType = VisualType.Line },           // a line
        new("Count") { SeriesType = VisualType.Scatter, SecondaryAxis = true }, // (2)!
    ],
};
  1. The type of the measures that set none.
  2. Points, against the right axis.
MeasureRef property SeriesType Bar, StackedBar, Line, Area or Scatter; null for the visual's type. SecondaryAxis Draws the measure against a second value axis, on the right.

Note

With a legend, every series of a measure keeps the measure's type. These settings only change the drawing: the query is the same, so changing them does not query the source again.

items.title: Conditional formatting
items.text: Each measure of a visual can have a format: colors by rules, a color scale, data bars or icons in tables and matrices; colored bars and shaded zones in charts.

items.title: In the designer
items.text: Select a measure's chip: the Formatting section edits its format. It only shows what the visual's type uses: on a chart, the rules (with their zone) and the scale; on a KPI, no scale or bars. What it hides is kept.

items.title: What a format holds
Colors
items.text: Colors are the theme's: ThemeColors.Accent, Success, Warning, Error, Muted. They follow light and dark themes and the control library, and are softened as backgrounds so that values stay readable. A custom #RRGGBB works too.

items.title: In charts
items.text:
Rules and the color scale color each bar, point and slice. A rule with Show its zone on charts (FormatRule.ShowOnChart) also shades its zone of the value axis, labelled with its condition.

  • Stacked bars are judged as a whole: a rule or a scale compares the total of the stack, and frames the stack in its color, so that the series keep their legend colors.
  • OxyPlot colors bars and slices one by one, but the points of lines by series only.

Compared with what is shown

The scale, the bars and the automatic thresholds compare a value with the cells shown, not with the totals. A matrix leaves its totals unformatted. A format only changes the drawing: the source is not queried again.

For connector and application authors

ValueStyler (Core) computes the ValueStyle of a value for any renderer, and the lookless FormattedValue control draws it in the built-in grids. ChartFormatting.For(request) gives a connector the color of each point (PointColor) and the zones (Bands); each ChartSeries carries the MeasureKey of its measure. LiveCharts2 uses OnPointMeasured and RectangularSection, OxyPlot RectangleAnnotation.

items.title: Legends
items.text: A chart places its legend from its size: on the right, then below, then hidden when there is no room. Users can pick another place.

items.title: Where
items.text:
In the designer's Visual section, Legend offers Automatic, Right, Bottom, Top, Left and Hidden.

LegendPosition = ChartLegend.Bottom,   // omitted from the JSON when Auto

A chosen side applies while the chart has room for it; otherwise the automatic place does.

items.title: By pages
items.text:
When a legend has more entries than its room shows, it shows them by pages: a small pager (◀ 2/5 ▶) appears in the corner next to it; its buttons and the mouse wheel turn the pages. The pager is a lookless control, ChartLegendPager, restyled like any other. Legends otherwise keep their charting library's look.

OxyPlot pies

OxyPlot names the slices of a pie around it rather than in a legend: hiding the legend drops those names.

items.title: Matrix
items.text:
A matrix crosses rows (up to four dimensions) with columns (one dimension), for each measure, and adds the totals of every row, every column and the whole.

DesignerCode

Pick Matrix in the gallery: its wells become Rows, Columns and Values.

new VisualDefinition
{
    Model = "sales",
    Type = VisualType.Matrix,
    Axis = [new("Product.Category"), new("Product.Name")],    // rows
    Legend = new("Date", DateGrain.Year),                     // columns
    Values = [new("Amount")],
};

items.title: Totals that stay right
items.text:
Each total is the measure computed on all the rows it covers, not a sum of cells: the total of a margin rate is the margin rate of the whole, an average stays an average. EasyBI runs one query per level of totals to get them.

  • Sort, Top N and the filters on measures choose the rows; the column totals then count those rows only.
  • Without columns, a matrix lists its rows with a total row.
  • Conditional formatting applies to the cells, not to the totals.

items.title: Interactions
items.text:
A click cross-filters the other visuals: a cell on its row and column, a row header or total on its row, a column total on its column.

For connector authors

VisualPipeline.PrepareAsync (with MatrixBuilder) hands the pivoted data to the renderer in RenderRequest.Matrix (MatrixData); a click reports a MatrixSelection. The built-in MatrixRenderer draws it in a grid styled like the table.

items.title: Comparisons over time
items.text: Each measure can be seen through time: its value the year before, the change since, or its total since the start of the year.

items.title: In the designer
items.text: Select a measure's chip: its Over time list offers the calculations. Drop the same measure twice to show it with and without one, as above.

items.title: In code
items.text:
Values =
[
    new("Amount"),
    new("Amount") { Time = TimeCalculation.PercentChangeFromPreviousYear },
],
Filters = [PeriodFilters.Relative("Date", FilterOperator.Current, DateGrain.Year)],   // this year
TimeCalculation Shows PreviousYear The value a year earlier ChangeFromPreviousYear The difference with a year earlier PercentChangeFromPreviousYear The difference in %; a KPI adds ▲ / ▼ YearToDate The running total since January 1st, along the date axis

items.title: How the previous year is computed
items.text:
The same query runs a second time with its dates shifted back one year (period filters, clicked periods), and its groups are matched with the first: each month with the same month a year earlier, per series. It works on any model, in VisualPipeline.PrepareAsync.

A period under way is compared with the same days

On February 15th, this year is compared with January 1st to February 15th of last year, not with the whole of last year, since there is no data after today. The same goes for the month under way, the last 12 months, or a range ending later.

A date is needed

The calculation needs a date on the axis or a date filter. Without either, it is empty.

items.title: Tooltips
items.text: Hovering a bar, a point, a slice or a step shows an EasyBI tooltip, the same with every connector: the category, then each series with its color and value.

items.title: What users set
items.text:
Per chart, in the designer:

  • the Tooltip well takes measures shown in the tooltip only (Quantity above): they are queried with the chart but draw no series;
  • the Tooltips section of the properties shows or hides the tooltips, the category, the series' names and each value's share of its series' total (%);
  • a custom text replaces the content, with fields between braces.
Field Is replaced by {category} The hovered category {series} The series' name {value} The hovered value, formatted {percent} Its share of its series' total {Quantity}, {Revenue}... Any measure of the chart or of the Tooltip well, by name or caption 
Tooltip = new TooltipSettings
{
    ShowPercent = true,
    Values = [new("Quantity")],
    Template = "{category}: {value} for {Quantity} sales", // (1)!
},
  1. An unknown field stays as typed.

items.title: Change the content
items.text:
EasyBIContext.TooltipOpening is raised before every tooltip opens, with the visual, the hovered category and series, and EasyBI's content (a TooltipContent: a Title, Items of label, value and color, or a Text). Replace it, or set it to null to show nothing:

context.TooltipOpening += (_, e) =>
{
    if (e.Visual.Model == "sales" && e.Content is { } content)
        e.Content = content with { Items = [.. content.Items, new TooltipItem("Target", Targets.For(content.Title))] };
};

items.title: Restyle it
items.text:
The frame is a standard ToolTip, so it takes your application's tooltip style. The content is drawn by a DataTemplate under ChartTooltips.TemplateKey:

<DataTemplate x:Key="{x:Static bi:ChartTooltips.TemplateKey}">
    <StackPanel>
        <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}" FontWeight="Bold" />
        <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding Items}" DisplayMemberPath="Value" />
    </StackPanel>
</DataTemplate>
For connector authors

Tooltips.Build(request, category, series) (EasyBI.Core) gives the default content of a RenderRequest, without a view.

items.title: Value labels
items.text: A visual can show its own text for values of a dimension: Paris area for Île-de-France, North for Nord.

items.title: In the designer
items.text: Select a dimension's chip: the Value labels section lets users pick a value (type to search among many), type its text and add it. Each label can be edited or removed.

items.title: In code
items.text:
Axis =
[
    new("Region") { Labels = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["Île-de-France"] = "Paris area", ["Nord"] = "North" } },
],

Keys are the values' invariant text. field.Display(value) and field.WithLabel(value, text) (EasyBI.Core) read and set them.

  • The labels apply everywhere in the visual: axis, groups, legend, tooltips, tables, matrices, the description of a selection.
  • Filters and cross-filtering keep the values themselves: renaming a value never changes what is filtered.
  • Dates have none: their periods follow their grain.
